links.comparator_used: No non-AI comparator arm; simulation of PCP review of AI drafts, with self-reported perception of workload versus usual practice
links.outcome: Clinician error detection and correction in AI-drafted patient portal replies, and perceived cognitive workload and safety
links.effect: 80% of PCPs agreed AI drafts reduced cognitive workload and 75% found them safe; each of 4 seeded errors was insufficiently addressed by 13-15 of 20 participants; 35-45% of erroneous drafts were submitted entirely unedited
links.tradeoff: New failure mode: clinician review often missed objective inaccuracies and potentially harmful omissions, creating patient safety risk
links.quote: While 80% of participants agreed AI drafts reduced cognitive workload and 75% found them safe, uncorrected errors highlight patient safety risks, underscoring the need for improved design, training, and error-detection mechanisms for AI tools.

design_hint: clinician review of AI-drafted patient message replies
